note: A summary of published views, not a recommendation. Crypto forecasts vary enormously and are often wrong — treat them as context only.

BTC.headline: Recovering from a weak first half, helped by money flowing back into Bitcoin ETFs, but a hawkish Fed caps it
BTC.context: About US$84,400 on 25 Sep 2026: up about 6% in a month but down about 23% over the year, and well below its record of about US$126,000 (Oct 2025).
supportive: US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about US$3.5 billion in August 2026, reversing about US$5.3 billion of outflows from January to July
Long-term holders stopped selling at the end of August
Regulation is getting clearer (the US GENIUS Act framework, access through 401(k) retirement accounts)
headwinds: The Fed raised rates in September 2026 and no cuts are expected this year, which is bad for risky assets
ETF outflows earlier in 2026 (about US$4 billion in June alone) show how quickly investor sentiment can reverse
Some analysts expect a further pullback based on Bitcoin's usual four-year cycle

forecasts.view: End-2026 US$82,000 base case / US$53,000 bear case (cut twice this year)

ETH.headline: Broke out of its downtrend in late August but is struggling to get past US$2,550
ETH.context: About US$2,450 at the start of September 2026, up from June lows of US$1,600–1,760 and roughly half its August 2025 peak of about US$4,958.
supportive: A 31% weekly gain in late August gave the first higher high of this cycle
Big investors and institutions are still buying on dips
headwinds: It hasn't broken above resistance around US$2,550 (its 50-week average), and the next level up is about US$2,920
Heavy borrowed (leveraged) bets could cause sharp swings if the price moves against them
The same rate and risk headwinds as Bitcoin

forecasts.view: More sideways first; support about US$2,200, resistance about US$2,800

sources.name: Yahoo Finance — What to expect from Ethereum in September 2026
